name: Short Straddle
summary: Sell a call and a put at the same strike and expiry for a large credit; maximum premium collection, undefined risk on both sides.

legs.strike_rule: Strike nearest spot (call delta closest to 0.50), or the delta-neutral strike if you want zero starting delta.

max_profit: total credit received, achieved only if the underlying finishes exactly at the strike
max_loss: UNDEFINED. Unlimited to the upside; (strike * 100) - credit to the downside.
breakevens: strike + credit per share and strike - credit per share

greeks.delta: near zero at entry, becomes large fast
greeks.gamma: strongly negative -- the worst negative gamma in the family
greeks.theta: strongly positive, the highest theta per contract of any two-leg structure
greeks.vega: strongly negative, -$30 to -$60 per vol point per 1-lot on an index ETF at 30 DTE

typical_dte: 45 DTE in, 21 DTE out, in the classic premium-selling framework
when_to_use: IV rank > 50 with an expectation of range-bound price action and vol contraction. Highest theoretical premium capture of any structure and, historically, positive expectancy on indices -- but the tail risk is real and unhedged.
entry_rules: BLOCKED ON THIS ACCOUNT. Requires uncovered (naked) short call and short put authority, which is Level 4. Alpaca offers Levels 1-3 only and rejects any multi-leg order whose legs are not covered within the same order. This strategy cannot be submitted and must be flagged as unavailable by the order router.
If it were ever enabled: IV rank > 50, no earnings inside the expiry, DTE 30-60, strike at the delta-neutral point.

Sizing would be by expected-move stress test: max loss at spot +/- 3 standard deviations must be <= 10% of equity, which on a $50k account means at most 1 contract on a sub-$100 underlying and zero on SPY.
Defined-risk substitute the system SHOULD trade instead: an iron butterfly (same short straddle with protective long wings), or a short strangle converted to an iron condor.
management_rules: If enabled: take profit at 25% of credit received (short straddles are managed at 25%, not 50%, because the risk is unbounded).
Stop: close the entire position if the loss reaches 2.0x the credit received.
Delta band: if net delta exceeds +/-0.30 per 1-lot, roll the tested side to restore neutrality, for a credit only.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: one of the two legs is always ITM at expiry by construction. This structure is guaranteed to be assigned if held. Close by 15:30 ET on expiry day, no exceptions.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close immediately whenever the ITM leg's extrinsic value < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close the call side before any ex-dividend date where the short call is ITM and extrinsic < 1.5 * dividend.
assignment_risk: Maximum in this family. One side finishes ITM essentially always. Assignment on the call side creates short stock; on the put side, long stock at the strike, which on a $50k account is an immediate margin breach for anything index-sized. There is no long leg to cover.
buying_power: Would be Reg-T naked margin: roughly 20% of the underlying value minus OTM amount, plus premium, per side, with only the greater side held. On SPY near $600 that is roughly $12,000-$14,000 per contract. Not available on Alpaca.
liquidity_needs: ATM legs are liquid, but the exit in a stress event is where the cost lands; require the underlying to have penny-wide ATM markets.
common_mistakes: Treating historical index short-straddle returns as a reason to run it undersized-margin; not having a mechanical stop; carrying it through an earnings gap; assuming 'I'll just take assignment' -- on a $50k account you cannot.
zero_dte_notes: Extremely high negative gamma; a 0DTE ATM short straddle can lose several multiples of its credit in minutes. Not tradable on this account anyway (Level 4). If a short-vol 0DTE expression is wanted, use a 0DTE iron butterfly instead.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
